title: Comparison of base-changed separable closures
statement: Let A and B be commutative local rings in one universe, let π:A → B be surjective, and let K and L be separable closures of their respective residue fields. Their A- and B-algebra structures factor through the residue fields as in [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Let H be extension of scalars defined by the ring pushout, as in [lem-sbc-surjective-quotient-base-change]. There is a B-algebra isomorphism H(K) ≅ L.

source.place: Tag 05WS, lemma-quotient-strict-henselization; parent proof step 1 (residue-field comparison)

proof.text: The induced residue-field map is injective because it is a homomorphism of fields, and surjective by lifting first through B → k(B) and then through π. Give L the k(A)-algebra structure obtained by composing this residue-field isomorphism with k(B) → L. Transfer separability along the base-field isomorphism and use transitivity. IsSepClosure.equiv then gives e:K ≅ L satisfying e(algebraMap A K a)=algebraMap B L (π a).

Set β:B → K equal to e inverse composed with B → L. The preceding equation gives βπ=A → K. The cocone with vertex K and legs id_K and β is a pushout: a map out is the K leg, its B compatibility is checked after the surjection π, and uniqueness follows from its K leg. Use uniqueness of pushouts, compose with e and transport through commAlgCatEquivUnder (including its unit isomorphism).
